title: Stroop color-word interference (Stroop, 1935), trial-wise by key
summary: How much does a colour word slow the naming of its ink? Each trial shows one colour square or colour word, and the subject presses the key for the ink (or, in the second task, for the word). Measure: time per item, conflicting against neutral items. Keys replace Stroop's spoken, timed sheets.
references: Stroop, J. R. (1935). Studies of interference in serial verbal reactions. Journal of Experimental Psychology, 18(6), 643–662.
Stroop, J. R. (1992). Studies of interference in serial verbal reactions. Journal of Experimental Psychology: General, 121(1), 15–23 (reprint of the 1935 article, public domain).
MacLeod, C. M. (1991). Half a century of research on the Stroop effect: An integrative review. Psychological Bulletin, 109(2), 163–203.

deviations.original: Each item named aloud (Exp. 2) or read aloud (Exp. 1); the experimenter followed on a key sheet (p. 17)
deviations.here: One key per colour (D F J K L by default), one item per trial
deviations.reason: alhazen has no voice key; a key response gives a per-item reaction time. Keys are an arbitrary learned mapping, not the habitual spoken response, which matters most for word reading (see 'Word reading')

deviations.original: A printed sheet of 100 items, ten lines of ten, held by the subject and read continuously (pp. 16-17)
deviations.here: One item per trial at the centre of a monitor, after a fixation point, in the sheet's reading order
deviations.reason: Trial-wise reaction times and per-item errors; the sheet's arrangement and its two forms are kept as the trial order

deviations.original: Time to read the whole sheet, by stop watch to a fifth of a second (p. 17)
deviations.here: Reaction time per item from the stimulus flip; the analysis also sums the items' times to the right key into a time per 100 items
deviations.reason: The summed time excludes eye movements between items, the fixation point and the inter-trial gap, so its absolute value is not comparable with Stroop's seconds; D over the control is the comparable quantity

deviations.original: Colour words read aloud, in black (RCNb) and in another ink (RCNd) (pp. 16-17)
deviations.here: A key press for the word named, black vs ink (task stroop-word-reading)
deviations.reason: Reading aloud is the over-learned response to a word; a key mapped to a word is not. Manual responses to words suffer colour interference (MacLeod, 1991), so this task is not expected to reproduce Stroop's near-null RCNd-RCNb difference and is not presented as Experiment 1

deviations.original: Subjects corrected their own errors aloud; in Exp. 2 each uncorrected error added twice the sheet's mean time per item (p. 17)
deviations.here: The item stays on screen after a wrong key until the right key or the deadline; a wrong key never corrected is UNCORRECTED and the analysis charges it twice the sheet's mean time per item
deviations.reason: The closest key-press equivalent of self-correction; the charge is Stroop's own rule

deviations.original: Every item was named in sequence
deviations.here: An item with no key before the deadline (NO_RESPONSE) is served again at the end of its block
deviations.reason: alhazen's rule that a trial without a measurement is re-served

deviations.original: None (spoken colour names need no training)
deviations.here: 25 trials of the control stimulus (squares, or black words) before block 1, five per colour
deviations.reason: An arbitrary five-key mapping has to be learned before the timed sheets

deviations.original: Inks printed on paper, daylight from the left; 14-point Franklin lower case type, squares from 24-point type (pp. 16-17)
deviations.here: Monitor colours on a light page-coloured background; Arial lower case
deviations.reason: A monitor replaces print; Franklin Gothic is not freely available, Arial is a sans serif of similar build

assumed.reason: Printed paper is implied, not described; slightly below full white to limit glare
The paper names the inks (p. 16) but gives no specification; saturated, mutually distinct and legible on the page colour
14-point type (p. 16) is about 4.9 mm; at an assumed 40 cm reading distance that is 0.7 dva
A solid square from 24-point type (p. 17) is about 5 mm wide; 0.75 dva at the same assumed 40 cm
The printed lists had no fixation point; a small point marks where the item will appear
A common foreperiod in trial-wise Stroop tasks
Reading was self-paced; a cap far above Stroop's slowest mean time per item (about 1.1 s)
Reading was continuous; a short gap between items

assumed.value: red D, blue F, green J, brown K, purple L
assumed.reason: Responses were spoken; one finger per colour on the home row, the same mapping for every subject

assumed.item: Assignment to the two block orders
assumed.value: Order A for odd subject numbers, B for even (CRC-32 parity for ids without a number)
assumed.reason: The paper assigned halves 'selected at random' (p. 17); a fixed rule makes the halves exact
Experiment 2 gives the order of tests, not of forms; Experiment 1's form pattern (p. 17) is reused

assumed.item: Forms per block, word reading, order B
assumed.reason: Experiment 1 gives the forms for order A only (p. 17); the same pattern is used for order B

assumed.value: Generated from the paper's rules with seed 1935
assumed.reason: The rules are the paper's (p. 16); the printed arrangement (Appendix B) is not in the copy read

assumed.value: One generated line obeying the sheet's rules
assumed.reason: The paper says a ten-word sample was read (p. 17), not which items

assumed.value: No feedback; the item stays on screen until the right key
assumed.reason: Stroop's subjects noticed their own errors and the experimenter pointed out uncorrected ones after the sheet (p. 17)

assumed.value: Self-paced: the next sheet starts when the subject presses SPACE
assumed.reason: The paper gives no interval between the four sheets of one sitting (p. 17)

tasks.title: Colour naming: squares vs incongruent words (Experiment 2)
tasks.summary: Give the INK colour by key. Four sheets of 100 items in the order NC, NCWd, NCWd, NC (or the reverse), each item a trial: fixation 500 ms, then the item until the right key.

parameters.name: background_rgb
parameters.label: Page colour
parameters.meaning: The window's background, PsychoPy rgb (-1..1). ASSUMED, not in the paper: printed paper.

parameters.name: colors
parameters.label: Ink colours
parameters.meaning: The five inks, PsychoPy rgb (-1..1). The paper names them (red, blue, green, brown, purple; p. 16); the coordinates are ASSUMED.

parameters.name: black_rgb
parameters.label: Black print
parameters.meaning: The ink of the RCNb control words (p. 16).

parameters.name: font
parameters.label: Typeface
parameters.meaning: Typeface for the words, lower case. DEVIATION: the paper used 14-point Franklin lower case type (p. 16).

parameters.name: letter_height_dva
parameters.label: Letter height
parameters.meaning: Text height (em) of the words. ASSUMED, not in the paper: 14-point type at an assumed 40 cm.

parameters.name: patch_size_dva
parameters.label: Square size
parameters.meaning: Side of the NC solid square. ASSUMED, not in the paper: a 24-point square (p. 17) at 40 cm.

parameters.name: fixation_size_dva
parameters.label: Fixation point size
parameters.meaning: Diameter of the fixation point. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: fixation_duration
parameters.label: Fixation duration
parameters.meaning: How long the fixation point is shown before each item. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: response_timeout
parameters.label: Response deadline
parameters.meaning: How long an item waits for the right key. ASSUMED, not in the paper (reading was self-paced).

parameters.name: iti
parameters.label: Inter-trial interval
parameters.meaning: Blank gap after each item. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: keys
parameters.label: Key for each colour
parameters.meaning: One key per colour. ASSUMED, not in the paper (responses were spoken).

parameters.name: require_correction
parameters.label: Correct every error
parameters.meaning: After a wrong key the item stays until the right key, as Stroop's subjects corrected their errors (p. 17). False ends the trial at the first key (outcome WRONG).

parameters.name: practice_trials
parameters.label: Practice items per test
parameters.meaning: Items of a practice sample before the first sheet of each test: Stroop's ten-word sample (p. 17).

parameters.name: key_practice_trials
parameters.label: Key-mapping practice
parameters.meaning: Control-stimulus trials before block 1 to learn the keys. DEVIATION: not in the paper.

parameters.name: sheet_items
parameters.label: Items per sheet
parameters.meaning: Items of each 100-item sheet served (p. 17). Test and simulate modes cut this to rehearsal.sheet_items.

parameters.name: block_order
parameters.label: Block order
parameters.meaning: A: control, interference, interference, control; B: the reverse (p. 17). by_subject: odd subject numbers A, even B (the rule is ASSUMED).

parameters.name: form_sequence
parameters.label: Form of each sheet
parameters.meaning: Which form (1, or 2 = reverse order) each of the four sheets uses. ASSUMED for Experiment 2 and for order B.

parameters.name: sheet_seed
parameters.label: Sheet seed
parameters.meaning: Seed of the generated sheet arrangement, built to the paper's rules (p. 16). ASSUMED: the printed arrangement is not in the copy read.

outcomes.name: CORRECT
outcomes.meaning: The first key was the right colour.

outcomes.name: CORRECTED
outcomes.meaning: A wrong key first, then the right key before the deadline (Stroop's self-correction).

outcomes.name: UNCORRECTED
outcomes.meaning: A wrong key never corrected before the deadline; the analysis charges it twice the sheet's mean time per item (p. 17).

outcomes.name: WRONG
outcomes.meaning: Only with require_correction false: the first key was wrong and ended the trial.

outcomes.name: NO_RESPONSE
outcomes.meaning: No bound key before the deadline; the item is served again at the end of its block.

events.name: RESPONSE_CUE
events.meaning: The item (square or word) shown; reaction time runs from this flip.

events.name: RESPONSE
events.meaning: The first bound key, right or wrong.

events.name: CORRECTION
events.meaning: The right key after a wrong one.
